prompt: The King on the Iron Throne, fifteen years after Robert's Rebellion
title: The Iron Throne
description: Fifteen years ago you took the Iron Throne in a rebellion against the last Targaryen king. The realm is at peace, but the crown owes 6 million gold dragons, much of it to House Lannister and the Iron Bank. Your Hand, Jon Arryn, has just died, and you must choose another. Across the Narrow Sea, the last children of the old dynasty are growing up in exile.

problems: The crown owes 6 million gold dragons and spends more than it collects.
Your Hand, Jon Arryn, is dead, and his office is empty.
The Targaryen heirs are looking for allies across the Narrow Sea.
No council votes on laws here. Everything you do is a royal decree, and each great house decides whether to go along.
The crown has no standing army. Before you call the banners, the great houses must give you at least 50 of 100 support.
If the great houses' support falls below their line, they warn you, then rise against you, as they rose against the last king on this throne.
You may send a killer after the Targaryen heirs. House Lannister and the Stormlands approve, and support in the North falls.
The Faith and the Iron Bank have no vote. The Faith can turn your own house against you, and the Bank can call in its loans.

holders.name: The great houses

persona.name: Eddard Stark
persona.role: Lord of Winterfell, Warden of the North
persona.bio: The Lords Paramount and their bannermen: Stark of the North, Arryn of the Vale, Tully of the Riverlands, Tyrell of the Reach, Martell of Dorne, Greyjoy of the Iron Islands. They raise every soldier the crown can call.
persona.tell: We bent the knee to your house once. A knee can straighten.

wants: The great houses, from Stark in the North to Martell in Dorne, want justice in their own lands and no royal hand on the men they raise.
redLines: Seizing a great house's lands or castle

persona.role: Lord of Casterly Rock, Warden of the West
persona.bio: The richest house in the realm: lords of Casterly Rock and the gold mines of the westerlands. Lord Tywin, your queen's father, holds much of the crown's debt.
persona.tell: Half the gold in your treasury came from Casterly Rock. We keep count.

wants: House Lannister wants the Hand's chain for one of its own and the crown's debt kept in its books.
responses: Keeps its men and gold at home

persona.name: Petyr Baelish

persona.tell: Your Grace's word is law. Our work is to make it a law the lords will follow.

wants: The small council wants a Hand you listen to and a treasury that does not run on borrowed gold.

persona.role: Lord of Dragonstone, master of ships
persona.bio: Your own house and the storm lords who rode with you: your brother Stannis on Dragonstone, your brother Renly at Storm's End, and their bannermen.

wants: House Baratheon and the Stormlands want your brothers given their due and the storm lords rewarded for the rebellion.
redLines: Inviting the Targaryen heirs home under a pardon

briefing.situation: Fifteen years ago you took the Iron Throne in a rebellion against the last Targaryen king. The realm is at peace, but the crown owes 6 million gold dragons, much of it to House Lannister and the Iron Bank. Your Hand, Jon Arryn, has just died, and you must choose another. Across the Narrow Sea, the last children of the old dynasty are growing up in exile.
briefing.room: No council votes on laws in the Seven Kingdoms. Your word is law, but the great lords decide whether to obey it, because they hold the land and the soldiers. Each decree that offends a house lowers its support. At the end of your reign five groups decide whether you keep the throne: the great houses with 30 of 100 votes, House Lannister and your own House Baratheon with 20 each, the small council and the smallfolk with 15 each.
briefing.you: You are the King, and no council votes on your word. You cannot pass laws, so you act by decree and your other royal powers. Your treasury starts at 22 of 100 because the crown lives on borrowed gold. The Faith cannot vote but can turn your own house against you, and the Iron Bank can call in its loans. The first act of your reign is the choice of a new Hand.
